problem: Write the complex number $z=-2+6\text{i}$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ giving $\theta $ in radians to $3$ decimal places.

feedback.problem: Write the complex number $z=-4-3\text{i}$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ giving $\theta $ in radians to $3$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the third quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi +|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{3}{4})| \\  & ≈\pi +0.643\,50… \\  & ≈3.785.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=5$ and $\theta =3.785$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=5\,{\text{e}}^{3.785\,\text{i}}\,.
$$
